messages:
emma: Heads up — found a reproducible auth bug when spinning up multiple AsyncClient instances with different creds. Looks like env-key rotation (we use a file watcher) ends up clobbering per-client creds so both clients end up using the same key. Repro below.

emma: Minimal repro:
```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
import asyncio

async def call(client, name):
    print(name, await client.generate("hi"))

async def main():
    # CLIENT_A reads API_KEY from env (rotating file watcher)
    client_a = AsyncClient()
    # CLIENT_B is constructed with explicit key
    client_b = AsyncClient(api_key="sk-clientb")
    await asyncio.gather(call(client_a, "A"), call(client_b, "B"))
```

emma: When the env watcher rotates the key between creating client_a and first request, both A and B show requests authenticated as the new env key (not sk-clientb).

raj: yikes. can you confirm whether this happens for sync Client too or only AsyncClient? also which SDK version?

emma: v0.12.3. I reproduced with sync Client too but async makes it easier to hit the race.

maria: do you pass any shared session or explicitly use the context manager?

emma: no shared session in the repro. clients are independent. tried with and without `async with` same effect.

oliver: sounds like the default auth provider is a module-level singleton that gets mutated on env change. workaround: always pass api_key to each client or construct with AuthProvider(api_key=...) until we fix.

raj: can you paste a short log trace showing the Authorization header for both requests? that will prove the client-level provider was swapped.

emma: pasted logs:
```
[2026-03-14T10:02:01Z] client=A AUTH=env:sk-rotated-abc123
[2026-03-14T10:02:01Z] client=B AUTH=env:sk-rotated-abc123  # expected sk-clientb
```

maria: ok thanks. filing an issue. this is likely the same bug we saw with credentials fallback precedence — the provider cache should be per-instance.

ci-bot: Created issue #4127: "auth provider singleton causes cross-client credential clobber during env rotation" and added label devex/regression. Assigned to @raj.

raj: assigned, I'll take a look. quick triage: suspect code in redwood.auth._get_default_provider() stores a single mutable provider at module scope and updates it on file watcher events. moving to instance-scoped provider + weakref cache should fix.

oliver: agree. also add an integration test that simulates env rotation while two clients exist. reproduction can live in devex/tests/test_auth_race.py.

emma: I'll write the failing test and open a draft PR. any preference for mocking the file watcher vs actually toggling an env file?

maria: mock the watcher callback to keep tests hermetic. example: use monkeypatch to swap the provider factory and invoke the rotate callback.

oliver: add a changelog entry and an SDK note: "If you pass api_key explicitly per-client you avoid this bug until upgrade".

emma: working on the test. will post PR link when ready. thanks! :partyparrot:

raj: thanks emma — initial patch idea: make AuthProvider creation happen in AsyncClient.__init__ if no explicit provider passed, never mutate module-level state after init. that should preserve existing behavior for consumers who rely on env rotation but avoid clobbering.

maria: also add type hints for the provider param in client init (we've had confusion about typing here). small follow-up: can we expose a helper `AuthProvider.from_env_watcher()` so callers can opt into rotation semantics per instance?

oliver: SGTM. API ergonomics is important — don't want folks to always have to implement workaround.

emma: PR opened: draft #4129 with failing test + initial fix. pinging for review.

ci-bot: Linked PR #4129 to issue #4127.

emma: marking this thread blocked on review, leaving reproduction snippets in the PR. thanks all :)
